p.src: Now this nine-thousand-three-hundred-li stretch of the mighty Yangzi joins three rivers in the distance: the Hanyang, the Xunyang, and the Yangzi. Running from Sichuan straight to the sea and connecting countless places along the way, it is therefore called the Long River of Ten Thousand Li. It divides the lands of Wu and Chu, and in midstream stand two mountains: one called Mount Jin and the other Mount Jiao. On Mount Jin stands a temple built all around the mountain, known as “the mountain within the temple”; on Mount Jiao stands a temple hidden in a hollow, its form unseen, known as “the temple within the mountain.” These two mountains rise from the river at the very border of Chu and Wu, with Yangzhou in Huainan East on one side and Runzhou in Zhexi on the other—the place now called Zhenjiang.

p.src: By then, Vanguard Commander Song Jiang's soldiers, horses, and warships were advancing by land and water. They had reached Huai'an and planned to assemble at Yangzhou. That day, Vanguard Song consulted in his tent with Military Adviser Wu Yong and the others. “The Great River is not far ahead, and enemy troops guard its southern bank. Who will go ahead to reconnoiter, learn what lies across the river, and find out whether we can advance?” Four fighting men stepped forward from below the commander's seat, all declaring themselves willing to go. The four were: Chai Jin, the “Little Whirlwind”; Zhang Shun, the “White Streak in the Waves”; Shi Xiu, the “Reckless Third Son”; and Ruan Xiaoqi, the “Living King of Hell.” Song Jiang said, “You four will divide into two parties: Zhang Shun with Chai Jin, and Ruan Xiaoqi with Shi Xiu. Go directly to Mounts Jin and Jiao and lodge there. Learn the true strength and disposition of the rebel lair at Runzhou, then come to Yangzhou and report.” The four took leave of Song Jiang. Each pair brought two attendants, disguised themselves as travelers, and set out first for Yangzhou. By this time, the people all along the road, hearing that the great army was coming to suppress Fang La, had moved their families into the villages to hide. In Yangzhou, the four parted company, each party laying in some dry provisions. Shi Xiu and Ruan Xiaoqi took two attendants and headed for Mount Jiao.

p.src: Chai Jin and Zhang Shun saw that below Mount Beigu the whole area was filled with blue and white banners, while many vessels stood in a single line along the shore. On the northern bank there was not so much as a single log. Chai Jin said, “There are houses along the Guazhou road, but no one lives in them, and there is no ferryboat on the river. How are we to learn what is happening across the water?” Zhang Shun said, “We must find a house where we can stay. Then watch while I take to the water, swim across to the foot of Mount Jin, and discover their true situation.” Chai Jin said, “That makes sense.” The four hurried to the riverbank and found several thatched cottages in a row, all tightly shut. They pushed at the doors, but none would open. Zhang Shun went around the side, lifted away a section of wall, and squeezed inside. There he saw a white-haired old woman rise from beside the stove. Zhang Shun asked, “Granny, why is your house shut up?” The old woman replied, “To tell you the truth, sir, we hear the imperial court has raised a great army to fight Fang La. This place of ours lies right in the path of wind and water. Those with homes here have all moved elsewhere to hide; only this old woman remains to watch the house.” Zhang Shun asked, “Where have the men of your household gone?” The old woman said, “He has gone to the village to look after the family.” Zhang Shun said, “There are four of us who wish to cross the river. Where might we find a boat?” The old woman said, “Where could you possibly get a boat? Recently, when Commissioner Lü heard that the great army was coming to fight him, he requisitioned every vessel and took them over to Runzhou.” Zhang Shun said, “We four have our own food. Just let us lodge in your house for two days. We will give you some silver for the room and cause you no trouble.” The old woman said, “You may stay, but I have no beds or mats.” Zhang Shun said, “We will make our own arrangements.” The old woman said, “Sir, I fear the great army may arrive at any moment!” Zhang Shun said, “We know how to keep out of their way.”

p.src: After watching from the riverbank for a while, Zhang Shun thought, “Commissioner Lü of Runzhou must often visit this mountain. Tonight I shall go there and will surely learn something.” He went back and discussed it with Chai Jin. “Now that we are here, there is not even a small boat to be found. How can we learn what is happening across the river? Tonight I will bundle up my clothes, balance two large silver ingots on my head, and swim straight to Jinshan Temple. I shall give some money to the monks, learn the true situation, and report back to our brother the Vanguard. You need only wait here.” Chai Jin said, “Finish the business quickly and return.”

p.src: That night, stars and moon shone together; the wind was mild, the waves calm, and water and sky merged into one. At dusk, Zhang Shun stripped to the waist, tightly girded on a pair of white silk swimming drawers, wrapped his headcloth and clothes around two large ingots of silver and fastened the bundle to his head, tucked a dagger at his waist, entered the water at Guazhou, and made straight for the middle of the open river. The water rose no higher than his chest, and he moved through it as though walking on dry land. When he had nearly reached the foot of Mount Jin, he saw a small boat moored beside a rocky peak. Zhang Shun climbed to its side, removed the bundle from his head, took off his wet garments, dried his body, put on his clothes, and sat down in the boat. He heard the night drum in Runzhou sounding the third watch. As Zhang Shun lay concealed in the boat and watched, he saw a small craft being rowed down from upstream. Zhang Shun looked at it and said, “There is something suspicious about that boat. There must be spies aboard!” He meant to cast off and take his boat out, but it was secured by a thick cable and had neither oar nor pole. Zhang Shun therefore stripped once more, drew his dagger, leapt back into the river, and made straight for the other craft. Two men aboard were working the oars, looking only toward the north bank. Taking no heed of the south, they rowed steadily on. Zhang Shun dived beneath the surface, came up alongside the craft, and seized its gunwale. With one sweep of his dagger, he slashed at the two oarsmen; they dropped their oars and toppled backward into the river. Zhang Shun had already sprung aboard. Two men scrambled out of the cabin. Zhang Shun raised his blade and struck one into the water; the other, terrified, fell backward into the cabin. Zhang Shun shouted, “Who are you? Where has this boat come from? Tell me the truth, and I will spare you!” The man replied, “Hero, hear my report. I am a steward in the household of Commander Chen of Dingpu Village outside Yangzhou. My master sent me across to Runzhou to pay my respects to Privy Commissioner Lü and offer provisions, which he accepted. He then sent an aide back with me to demand fifty thousand shi of polished grain and three hundred boats as tribute.” Zhang Shun said, “What is that aide’s surname and given name? Where is he now?” The steward replied, “The aide’s surname is Ye and his given name is Gui. He is the man you just struck into the river.” Zhang Shun said, “And what is your surname? What is your name? When did you cross over to pay your respects? What is aboard the boat?” The steward replied, “My surname is Wu and my given name is Cheng. I crossed the river on the seventh day of the first month this year. Privy Commissioner Lü ordered me to proceed directly to Suzhou, where I met the Imperial Prince, Third Prince Fang Mao. I received three hundred identifying banners, together with my master Commander Chen’s patent of office appointing him prefect of Yangzhou and formally granting him the title of Zhongming Dafu. There are also a thousand livery coats and an official dispatch from Privy Commissioner Lü.” Zhang Shun asked again, “What is your master’s surname and name? How many men and horses does he command?” Wu Cheng replied, “He has several thousand men and more than a hundred horses. He has two sons of his own, both exceptionally formidable: the elder is Chen Yi, and the younger Chen Tai. My master, the commander, is called Chen Guan.” After Zhang Shun had questioned him thoroughly about every detail of their business and intentions, he killed Wu Cheng with a single stroke and cast him into the water as well. He took up the oar at the stern and rowed straight to Guazhou.

p.src: Hearing the beat of an oar, Chai Jin hurried out to look and saw Zhang Shun approaching in a boat. Chai Jin asked what had happened, and Zhang Shun related the entire affair. Chai Jin was delighted. He entered the cabin and brought out a bundle of documents, three hundred red silk identifying flags, and a thousand livery coats of assorted colors, arranging them into two shoulder-loads. p.src: Yan Qing now assumed the local speech of Zhejiang and greeted a manor servant, saying, “Is General Chen at home?” The servant asked, “Where have you travelers come from?” Yan Qing replied, “From Runzhou. After crossing the river, we took the wrong road and wandered about for half a day before asking our way here.” Hearing this, the servant led them into a guest room, had them set down their loads, and took Yan Qing to the rear hall to meet General Chen. Yan Qing at once bowed low and said, “Ye Gui presents himself before you!” When the bow was finished, General Chen asked, “Where have you come from, sir?” Speaking in a Zhejiang accent, Yan Qing said, “Only after the idlers have withdrawn shall I dare speak to Your Excellency.” General Chen said, “These men are all my trusted confidants. Speak freely.” Yan Qing said, “This humble man is surnamed Ye and named Gui, and serves as an aide in Privy Councillor Lü’s command. On the seventh day of the first month, the Privy Councillor received Wu Cheng’s secret letter and was greatly pleased. He specially ordered me to escort Wu Cheng to Suzhou to meet the Imperial Brother, the Third Prince, and fully explain Your Excellency’s intentions. The Third Prince sent a memorial to the throne, whereupon an official patent was issued appointing Your Excellency Prefect of Yangzhou. As for the two Court Attendants, their ranks and titles will be settled after they have met Privy Councillor Lü. We intended to send Wu Cheng back, but unexpectedly he caught a chill and fell ill, leaving him unable to travel. Fearing that this great affair might be delayed, the Privy Councillor specially ordered me to deliver Your Excellency’s patent of office, together with his dispatches, official seals and passes, three hundred signal flags, and one thousand uniforms. On the appointed day and hour, Your Excellency is to take the grain and boats to the riverbank at Runzhou and hand them over.” He then produced the patent and dispatches and handed them to General Chen. After reading them, Chen was overjoyed. He hastily set out an incense table, faced south, and gave thanks for the imperial favor; then he summoned Chen Yi and Chen Tai to meet the visitors. Yan Qing told Xie Zhen and Xie Bao to bring out the uniforms and signal flags and deliver them in the rear hall; General Chen then invited Yan Qing to take a seat. Yan Qing said, “I am merely a common runner. How could I dare sit in Your Excellency’s presence?” General Chen replied, “You were sent here by my gracious patron across the river, and you have brought this humble official his patent of appointment. How could I dare treat you lightly? Please sit for the present; there is no harm in it.” After repeatedly declining out of courtesy, Yan Qing sat down at a respectful distance. General Chen ordered wine brought and raised a cup to Yan Qing; but Yan Qing declined, saying, “By a heavenly vow, I do not drink wine.” After General Chen had drunk two or three rounds, both his sons came forward to congratulate their father and offer him wine. Yan Qing signaled with his eyes for Xie Zhen and Xie Bao to act. Xie Bao drew from his clothes a drug that made no distinction between lord and subject and, while no one was watching, slipped it into the wine pot. Yan Qing then rose and said, “Though I, Ye Gui, brought no wine across the river, allow me to borrow Your Excellency’s wine and delicacies to offer my congratulations.” He poured a great brimming cup, presented it to General Chen, and urged him to drain it. Next he offered Chen Yi and Chen Tai a cup apiece, and each drank. Yan Qing also persuaded each of the trusted manor servants present to drink a cup. At a slight pursing of Yan Qing’s lips, Xie Zhen went outside, found a light, took out a signal flag and signal charge, and fired the charge before the manor. The commanders were already waiting on either side; the moment they heard the signal charge, they advanced to give support. Inside the hall, when Yan Qing saw them fall one after another, he drew a short blade from his clothes and joined Xie Bao in striking; before long, every head had been cut off. Outside the manor gate, ten valiant men raised a clamor and fought their way in from the front. Those ten officers were Lu Zhishen the Flowery Monk, Wu Song the Pilgrim, Shi Jin the Nine-Dragoned, Yang Xiong the Sick Guan Suo, Li Kui the Black Whirlwind, Xiang Chong the Eight-Armed Nezha, Li Gun the Great Sage Who Soars to Heaven, Bao Xu the God of Death, Yang Lin the Brocade Leopard, and Xue Yong the Sick Tiger. How could the manor servants at the gate possibly withstand them? Within, Yan Qing, Xie Zhen, and Xie Bao had already carried out the heads of General Chen and his sons;

u.src: Yan Qing now assumed the local speech of Zhejiang and greeted a manor servant, saying, “Is General Chen at home?”
The servant asked, “Where have you travelers come from?”
Yan Qing replied, “From Runzhou.
After crossing the river, we took the wrong road and wandered about for half a day before asking our way here.”
Hearing this, the servant led them into a guest room, had them set down their loads, and took Yan Qing to the rear hall to meet General Chen.
Yan Qing at once bowed low and said, “Ye Gui presents himself before you!”
When the bow was finished, General Chen asked, “Where have you come from, sir?”
Speaking in a Zhejiang accent, Yan Qing said, “Only after the idlers have withdrawn shall I dare speak to Your Excellency.”
General Chen said, “These men are all my trusted confidants. Speak freely.”
Yan Qing said, “This humble man is surnamed Ye and named Gui, and serves as an aide in Privy Councillor Lü’s command.

On the seventh day of the first month, the Privy Councillor received Wu Cheng’s secret letter and was greatly pleased. He specially ordered me to escort Wu Cheng to Suzhou to meet the Imperial Brother, the Third Prince, and fully explain Your Excellency’s intentions.
The Third Prince sent a memorial to the throne, whereupon an official patent was issued appointing Your Excellency Prefect of Yangzhou.
As for the two Court Attendants, their ranks and titles will be settled after they have met Privy Councillor Lü.
We intended to send Wu Cheng back, but unexpectedly he caught a chill and fell ill, leaving him unable to travel.

p.src: When Song Jiang heard that General Chen had been killed, he conferred with Wu Yong on advancing the army. They packed their baggage, took leave of Commander-in-Chief Zhang, and led the main force in person to General Chen’s manor. There they assigned officers to the vanguard and put their plan into operation aboard the boats, while sending men to hurry the warships onward. Wu Yong said, “Choose three hundred swift boats and fly on each the banners surrendered by Fang La. Have one thousand soldiers put on the uniforms, while the remaining three or four thousand wear assorted clothing.” More than twenty thousand men were concealed aboard the three hundred boats. Mu Hong was also ordered to impersonate Chen Yi, and Li Jun to impersonate Chen Tai, each seated aboard a large boat, while the other boats were assigned among the officers.
